newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dah Sing to sell 20 pct of home loans.
newsitem.headline: Dah Sing to sell 20 pct of home loans.

text.p: Dah Sing Bank plans to bundle up and sell about 20 percent of its residential mortgages through a US$300 million cross-border mortgage securitisation, the bank said on Thursday.

"About 20 percent of our mortgage pool will be now put off balance sheet," Gary Wang, general manager and financial controller with Dah Sing Bank and its parent, Dah Sing Financial Holdings told a briefing.
Executives at the bank said they planned to launch the securitisation through a special-purpose company, Hong Kong SAR Residential Mortgages Ltd.
They said the Cayman Islands-incorporated Hong Kong SAR Residential Mortgages, would pay Dah Sing Bank HK$2.32 billion for a pool of mortgages.
Mortgage securitisations involve issuing securities backed by mortgages to investors.
The interest and principal payments to investors are backed by the interest and principal payments made by the house-buyers on their mortgages.
Dah Sing Bank chairman David Wong said the transaction was the largest cross-border, mortgage-backed or asset-backed deal originated in Asia, excluding Japan.
Ronald Carstairs, vice-chairman and managing director of Dah Sing Bank, said freeing up the balance sheet would give the bank more freedom in its lending decisions.
"Freeing up the balance sheet clearly will give us scope to aim our arrows in the direction in which we wish to point them," said Carstairs.
Carstairs said Dah Sing Bank wanted to step up retail activities, including credit card activities, as well as in traditional areas like trade financing and hire purchase.
Residential mortgages constitute about 45 percent of the bank's lending portfolio, against only two percent for credit cards and four percent for personal loans.
Trade and commercial finance total 28 percent and hire purchase finance 18 percent, and the remainder comes from commercial mortgages.
Mark Bucknall, head of capital markets with HSBC Markets, which is arranging the deal, said the securitisation in Asia was still dwarfed by markets like the united States.
"In 1996, approximately US$150 billion was raised by North American in the domestic U.S. market. This volume is nearly three times what it was just five years ago," Bucknall said.
"In Asia, we estimate that US$1 billion was raised during 1996. And during 1997 the total figure will be nearer the US$2 billion mark," Bucknall said.
The issue is expected to carry AAA/Aaa ratings from Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service thanks to credit enhancements from Asia Ltd and CapMAC.
The issue is expected to be launched on June 18, and listed in Luxembourg.
